in_arabic.name: ماوية
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من الماء، يدل على الهدوء و السكينة
in_arabic.long_meaning: ماوية هو اسم علم مؤنث من أصل عربي، مشتق من كلمة الماء، ويدل على الهدوء والسكينة. وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة آل عمران: 'وَمَاوِيَاتٍ مِّن فَاكِهَةٍ وَنَخْلٍ وَرُمَّانٍ' (آل عمران: 123). ويعتبر هذا الاسم من الأسماء الجميلة والخفيفة التي تحمل معاني جميلة في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: ماویہ
in_urdu.meaning: پانی سے ماخوذ، سکون اور آرام کا مطلب
in_urdu.long_meaning: ماویہ ایک علم اسم ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے۔ یہ پانی سے نکلا ہے اور سکون، آرام اور ہڈوء کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ اسلامی تقویم میں، یہ نام خاص معانی رکھتا ہے کیونکہ یہ قرآن مجید میں مختلف آیات میں ذکر ہوا ہے، جیسے کہ آل عمران میں: 'وَمَاوِيَاتٍ مِّن فَاكِهَةٍ وَنَخْلٍ وَرُمَّانٍ' (آل عمران: 123)۔

in_hindi.name: माविया
in_hindi.meaning: जल से व्युत्पन्न, शांति और सुकून का अर्थ
in_hindi.long_meaning: माविया एक सुंदर और अर्थपूर्ण नाम है जो जल से व्युत्पन्न है। यह नाम शांति, सुकून और आराम की भावना को दर्शाता है। इस्लामी परंपरा में, यह नाम महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह कुरआन में विभिन्न स्थलों पर उल्लिखित है, जैसे कि सूरा आल इमरान में: 'وَمَاوِيَاتٍ مِّن فَاكِهَةٍ وَنَخْلٍ وَرُمَّانٍ' (आल इमरान: 123)।

in_pashto.name: ماویا
in_pashto.meaning: د اوبو څخه اخیستل شوی، د سولې او ارامتی معنی
in_pashto.long_meaning: ماویا د یوې ښکلې نجلۍ نوم دی چی د اوبو څخه اخیستل شوی دی. دا نوم د سولې، ارامتی او هډو معنی لری. په اسلامي کلتور کی، دا نوم د پام وړ دی ځکه چی دا په قرآن کریم کی په ډیرو ځایونو کی راغلی دی، لکه څنګه چی په سورة آل عمران کی: 'وَمَاوِيَاتٍ مِّن فَاكِهَةٍ وَنَخْلٍ وَرُمَّانٍ' (آل عمران: 123)۔

in_english.name: Mawiya
in_english.meaning: Derived from water, symbolizing calmness and serenity
in_english.long_meaning: Mawiya is a beautiful and meaningful name derived from the Arabic word for 'water'. It symbolizes calmness, serenity, and peacefulness. In Islamic tradition, this name holds significance as it is mentioned in the Quran, specifically in Surah Al Imran: 'And shades and fruits and palm trees with softened 'stems' (Al Imran: 123). The name Mawiya reflects tranquility and is considered a lovely choice for a child, embodying the soothing qualities of water.

data.cultural_impact: Mawiya is a name of Arabic origin, deeply rooted in Islamic history as the name of one of the most significant figures in early Islamic history - Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan. He was the fifth caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate, ruling from 661 to 680 AD. Muawiya's reign marked the end of the Rashidun period, and the beginning of the Umayyad Caliphate, which transformed the Islamic world into a vast, powerful empire. This new era was characterized by a distinction in courtly culture, art, and literature. The application of the name Mawiya in today's context can serve as a reminder of the grace, elegance, and transformative power in leadership.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Mawiya lies in its original meaning: 'the one who is graceful and elegant.' As a believer, focusing on the spiritual essence of Mawiya, would mean striving to embody the qualities of grace and elegance in one's character and actions. These qualities are particularly relevant in the Islamic context, as they reflect honorable and desirable traits. By emulating Mawiya's spirit of grace and refinement, one can improve their ethical character, enhancing their spiritual growth in their religious journey.

historical_references.reference:
Mawiya was the caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate from AD 661 to 680. He succeeded his father-in-law, Muawiya I, and was the last Umayyad ruler of the Umayyad dynasty before the Umayyad caliphate took power.
Context: Mawiya came to power after the First Fitna (Civil War) following the death of Prophet Muhammad.
historical_references.context: Last Umayyad ruler of the Rashidun Caliphate, succeeded Muawiya I and came to power after the First Fitna (Civil War) following the death of Prophet Muhammad.

historical_references.reference:
Mawiya was also a prominent military commander and governor during the reign of Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab. He was Umar's governor in Syria from 634 to 640, and was instrumental in expanding the Muslim territories in Syria and Palestine.
Context: Mawiya was a military commander and governor under Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab.
historical_references.context: Prominent military commander and governor under Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab, instrumental in expanding Muslim territories in Syria and Palestine.

modern_usage.modern_context: Mawiya, also known as Muawiya I or Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, was an Arab Muslim political and military leader who became the second Umayyad caliph (r. 661–680). He is often considered the founder of the Umayyad Caliphate. Today, Mawiya is primarily remembered as a significant figure in Islamic history, and his name is mentioned frequently in discussions about early Islamic politics and governance. He is a topic of debate among scholars and is discussed on various platforms such as Wikipedia, Twitter, and Reddit where users explore his role in Islamic history and the political and social implications of his rule.
